newsitem.title: INDIA: MIFFED INDIAN POLITICIAN ASSIGNED MORE CLOUT.
newsitem.headline: MIFFED INDIAN POLITICIAN ASSIGNED MORE CLOUT.

text.p: India's government on Thursday moved to mollify its junior petroleum minister, whose group is an influential partner in the ruling coalition, by assigning him greater responsibilities.
Newspapers reported earlier on Thursday that junior petroleum minister T.R. Baalu might resign after the government unveils a long-awaited increase in oil product prices.
Baalu was not immediately available for comment.

"Baalu's threat of resigning from the government is due to the allocation of duties and not because of any concern over the proposed price hike," said a Petroleum Ministry official who did not wish to be identified.

Baalu, a first-time federal minister, belongs to the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party which has 17 deputies in parliament's lower house. The ruling United Front coalition has a minority of 178 lawmakers in the 545-seat house.

Baalu was inducted in June 1996 as the junior petroleum minister by former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who himself held the senior portfolio and effectively left the running of the key ministry to Baalu.

Baalu was effectively demoted last April when Inder Kumar Gujral took over as prime minister after Deve Gowda's ouster. Gujral named Janeshwar Mishra as the senior petroleum minister and Baalu was assigned a lesser set of responsibilities including oil conservation and industry safety.

In yet another sign of the fractures in the fragile ruling coalition, Mishra on Thursday moved to re-assign important policy issues such as coal-bed methane policy and the New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP) to Baalu.
The petroleum ministry official said Baalu has also been asked to screen senior appointments and "all policy matters requiring cabinet approval".
